nodes.speakerLine: The Forge is cold today. Bring me something worth heating.
Respecs. Crafting. Tier work, when you find gear worth the risk. The Forge handles every change you'll ever make to yourself — remember that.
So I heard. The Quartermaster counts what comes back, and this time the count was right. That buys you a hearing here, when you have something to bring.
...Yes. Built before the militia captured the shipment. I remember being manufactured. Ask me what you actually came to ask, or don't.
(A long pause. The Forge hums.) ...Bring me something worth heating, Breaker.
(The Forge is still cold. Kess does not look up.) You came back. That's more than most.

(Kess turns a cold crucible with one hand.) Feedstock. Vestige residue burns, and the spill carries more of it than the ground can rot. Six of them. Bring me what's left when they drop — I'll know the weight when you walk in.
Not the weight yet. Six carcasses' worth. The Forge has waited years — it can wait an afternoon.
(Kess does not weigh anything. Kess already knows.) That's the weight. The Forge takes it. ...It's warmer in here now. Remember that, next time you find something worth heating.
(The Forge is lit. Low, but lit.) You did that. Now find me something worth it.
Ammo's on the shelf, gear's in the crates. You breaking things or buying things?

choices.text: What's this about a bad rift?

nodes.speakerLine: Requisitions, then. Anything your class is cleared for, I can sign out — one token a piece, and I don't take Riftglass for it. Rift work earns the tokens; I just hold the keys.
The spill out past the pad keeps regrouping. Thin it out, and put that elite down while you're at it. I count what comes back — that's the job.
Count's not right yet. The spill's still moving and that elite's still upright. Come back when both of those stop being true.
Count's right. Spill's thinned and the elite's down. You did the job and you came back to say so, which is rarer than the first part.
Contract's closed and you've been paid. There'll be more — the spill always comes back. Ammo's still on the shelf.
Second contract. The spill keeps regrouping — same ground, same hours — and the marked ones are up front now, every time. Three of them, down. I want to see if the next count sheet reads different.
Count's short. The marked don't fall easy — that's why the contract says three and not thirty. Come back when the sheet's full.

Count's right. Three marked, three down. ...Off the record: spills drift. This one doesn't. Same ground, every time, like something's taking a measurement. The sheet doesn't have a box for that, so it's going down as weather.
Contract's closed, paid in full. Sheet still says weather. Weather doesn't hold formation.

Last one on my sheet, and I don't love writing it. Command flagged a rift out past the far ground — didn't close clean, their words. Everything it lets through comes up marked. Sweep it: five of the marked, and whatever's biggest goes down first.
Sweep's not done. Five of the marked, and the count's honest or it's nothing. Same as always — I count what comes back.

Five down, and you walked back in to say so. Good count. ...That rift's still out there. Didn't close clean — Command's words, not mine. It's gone up the chain, and what goes up the chain comes back down with a name and a Breaker attached. Sleep while you can.
Sheet's clear. First time since you signed in. Restock while it lasts — when that name comes back down the chain, it'll be yours.
New contact at the Fernhall rail trench. One, moving badly. The patrol says it does not look like the others. Get eyes on it before anything else comes through.
Past the rail span, in the trench. One contact. Find out what we are dealing with, then bring the report back yourself.
The rail trench. I need the contact accounted for, not another count from the spill.
A uniform. Rank markings, repairs. Not ours. ...No, I do not have an explanation ready. Leave the details in the report. Every one of them.

choices.text: It was wounded. It still came at me.

nodes.speakerLine: The opening beyond the rail trench is holding steady. More shapes on the other side, moving together. That contact came from somewhere. We need to see where.
Take the Breach door beyond the rail trench. Clear a way through the marshalling ground and put its commander down. Then come back. We are done calling this weather.
The Breach, beyond the rail trench. Its commander is the objective. Clearing another local rift will not do this job.
A field commander. Positions, signals, orders. Somebody on the other side knows how a fight works. Your report goes up intact. Your requisition is here; take it before they find another commander.
A voice came through the far side of the Breach. Still answering. Take the new passage; find whoever is left before the signal goes quiet.
Earth, without the works or the stacks. The Vestiges reached it anyway. If that voice belongs to a person, bring them inside the Anchor. Don't leave them waiting out there.
The Earth passage is ready. Find the voice, clear a path, and get them through. The Anchor is the part that matters.
They're still themselves. Give them a place to sit. The reports can wait.
The Breach is open for another sweep if you need one. You already earned the requisition. For now, restock and make something of what you learned.
You heard me. Good. I was starting to forget the next word. There were no factories here. The things came all the same. Is there somewhere the noise stops?

choices.text: [Escort] Stay close. I'll get you to the Anchor.
[Leave] Wait here. I'll clear the way.

nodes.speakerLine: I remember you. I can still walk. Tell me when to follow.
I can see the opening. Please. All the way through.
It's quiet. I thought I'd forgotten what quiet was. Those people outside, the ones who couldn't answer anymore... you did what you had to. Can I sit here?
I remember the path to my house. Every stone. I don't need to tell it to you yet, do I?
The instruments are still running. Give me a moment.
The person you brought back described a world without industry. This signal comes from one that solved the problems ours could not. There is almost nothing left of it.

I worked with Rior on the transfer array. Those are our couplings in the survey image. Someone used them to take that Earth apart. Recover the working fragment at the extraction rig; I can reconstruct the routing from it.
The fragment sits inside the stripped Earth's extraction rig. Bring back the assembly, not a transcription.

These are working notes: 'Transfer demand exceeds local renewal. Receiving timelines must close their draw before the source can recover.' That correction was in the original model. I am leaving the extraction stage disconnected.
One coordinate still resolves to an inhabited Earth. Their array stopped before ours did. Go there. See what remained.
The assembly is ready. The control face shows both outcomes. I will not choose for you.
The receiver is quiet. I have kept the names we brought inside.
There are still voices on the receiver. I am leaving the extraction stage disconnected.
A transfer assembly remains bolted to the extraction rig. Its working slate still records the draw from this Earth.
Clear the nearby Vestige guards, then approach the rig to recover the fragment.
You stop at the same distance I did. We shut their array down here. The town is still ours. Come and sit a moment; you look as if you have been walking for days.
There is a spare place at the table. It will be here when you come back.

SEAL closes every rift permanently. This timeline is safe; every timeline beyond the rifts, and every refugee not inside an Anchor, is erased as if they never existed.

HOLD leaves the doors open. Those people can still be reached. The transfer method remains usable, including by those who stripped the other Earth.

Both choices lead into the same endgame. The decision is available at level 50.

choices.text: [SEAL] Make this timeline safe. Erase the worlds beyond.
[HOLD] Keep the refugees reachable. Leave the method intact.

nodes.speakerLine: SEAL selected. The receiver is silent. The names of those inside the Anchor remain.
HOLD selected. The receiver still carries living voices. The work of reaching them continues.
The assembled device requires level 50. Your recovered work is safe; return when you reach level 50 to choose SEAL or HOLD.
I don't go back and I don't go forward. I just count what comes through.
The substation side. They come up through it and I can't watch both ends. Six of them and the count goes back to something I can live with.
Substation flank. Six. I'll be here — I'm always here.
Still hearing them. Whatever you're doing, it isn't finished.
Quiet on that side. First time this week.
Here. It came through the tear and I've no use for it. You will.
The terminal is lost. Get me across the apron to Maintenance Hangar. Stay close and clear the route. If this attempt fails, regroup here.

choices.text: I will guide you. Follow me.

nodes.speakerLine: Maintenance Hangar is secure. I can take it from here.
